transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-09-08
- Time: 10:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood CSM), Samir (Peregrine VP Eng), Lena (NetOps), Ben (Security), Tara (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync for week 5 of the private POC. Focus areas: kernel compatibility with Peregrine's quantized model, observed p95 latency spike on the 30th, routing/fallback behavior during short egress blips, and a small canary window for kernel upgrade. Action items and security follow-ups captured at the end.

Topics (auto-gen, may be fuzzy):
- Kernel compatibility testing
- Quantized model (INT8/AMP) performance
- VPC egress and routing fallbacks
- KMS rotation and SOC2 expectations
- Canary plan + smoke tests

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round robin who we've got?
[00:07] Samir (Peregrine): Samir here, VP Eng, I'm joined by Lena and Ben and Tara. thanks.
[00:12] Maya: perfect. Diego, can you kick us off with the kernel-compat status?
[00:16] Diego (Redwood): yeah sure. so we ran the baseline on the quantized model you sent last week, the int8 export. initial pass looked good for throughput, but we hit a mismatch on the attention kernel when sequence length went above 1K. it manifested as a small latency tail — p99 jumping to ~1.8s on our infra emulation.
[00:35] Tara (Peregrine): mmh, interesting. our primary traffic is 512 tokens 85% of the time, but we do have long context for doc-ops, yeah.
[00:43] Lena: those spikes align with the long context sessions we saw in the flow logs friday. we thought maybe it was routing into a standby node.
[00:49] Diego: there's two things. one is the kernel selection path — when seq len > 1024 our runtime falls back to a generic matmul kernel that isn't as optimized for fused attention, which increases tokens overhead. second is batching alignment; some of your traffic patterns create small micro-batches which kill perf.
[01:12] Ben (Security): just to pause — before we dive deeper, do we have any risk on key material? the model artifacts are in our S3 and KMS wrapped, we need to ensure pods won't accidentally stage keys.
[01:23] Nina (Redwood): re key material, on the private deployment we do not access your KMS directly — the customer-managed KMS integration means keys never leave your environment. Diego, can you confirm we didn't pull key files?
[01:34] Diego: correct, we only referenced model blobs via the customer's signed link in the test harness; no key material was downloaded to Redwood-managed control plane.
[01:41] Ben: ok that'll be in writing please, we have compliance gating.
[01:44] Maya: noted, we'll circulate the KMS integration note and an architecture diagram.

[01:50] Diego: back to perf. we can push a kernel compatibility matrix — try the AMP path, try INT8 low-precision fused kernels, and a fallback list. We'll also run mutli-batch simulations using your 10k sample file if you can provide it.
[02:06] Samir: we can provide a 10k sample but it's scrubbed, there are PHI concerns so we'll share a synthetic representative file by EOD Monday.
[02:13] Tara: also, I want to mention that when we tested internal infra we saw memory pressure causing occasional evictions, could that interact?
[02:20] Diego: yes, memory patterns can flip kernel choice too. if the KV cache allocation grows unexpectedly the runtime will switch code paths. we should capture kv cache hit ratios.
[02:30] Lena: on the routing side, the main issue we observed was an egress blip on 08/30 around 03:14 UTC — that triggered a route failover and we saw a small spike in re-tries.
[02:39] Maya: can you share the traceroute or the flow logs for that window?
[02:42] Lena: yes, exporting those now, we'll drop them into the shared drive.
[02:46] Ben: question about fallback semantics: during a route failover does Redwood automatically swap to a smaller model or to a different region? we need clarity for SRE playbooks.
[02:56] Diego: current default policy for private is region-aware fallback: first we attempt local variant (which is usually same model but lower batch/concurrency), then if capacity constrained we fall back to a cpu-light variant or a smaller quantized model if you've opted in. we can customize the policy per route.
[03:15] Samir: hmm, we worry about quality regression if you auto-fallback to a smaller model for certain calls — we need a deterministic fallback policy and an approval hook.
[03:23] Nina: that's reasonable. we can implement an approval webhook so your SREs and ML team get notified and can control auto-rollback.
[03:30] Tara: would that add latency? webhooks could fail.
[03:33] Diego: webhook is async and non-blocking; we won't block inference on webhook response. it's just an alert/approval path for ops.
[03:40] Ben: security follow-up — do you have SOC2 certs for the private control plane? our compliance will need evidence about logging and audit trails.
[03:48] Maya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. for private deployment we provide audit logs and we've documented retention options in our security pack. we'll send the security deck with the SOC2 summary and the audit log endpoints.
[03:59] Ben: good. also key rotation cadence — we rotate monthly and perform forced rotation during incident. can Redwood support automated re-wrap?
[04:06] Diego: yes, we support customer-managed KMS with re-wrap if you provide the key policy. we'll confirm supported KMS providers in the follow-up.
[04:14] Samir: desired SLA: p50 < 45ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 400ms for our 512 token traffic. can you hit that on the dedicated pilot infra?
[04:24] Diego: on our baseline with your traffic profile tuned for steady 512 tokens and 8-16 batch sizes, we can get p50 ~ 30ms p95 ~ 160ms but p99 depends heavily on long-context and micro-batch alignment. we need the sample traces to model it.
[04:39] Samir: okay, if you can reproduce our p99 at scale that's a go.
[04:44] Maya: let's be explicit on acceptance criteria — Diego can produce a perf run that simulates your traffic and shows p50/p95/p99 along with batch distributions; Samir to sign off.

[04:52] Diego: technical note: for the kernel upgrade we recommend a 2-hour canary window with a 30-minute ramp and a 30-minute observe stage. smoke tests include token-level correctness tests for a few prompts, KV cache warm-up, and a synthetic spike run.
[05:09] Lena: 2 hours is fine, but we need the list of smoke tests so we can run them on our side.
[05:13] Nina: I'll own the smoke test checklist and schedule.
[05:16] Ben: and we need rollback triggers — CPU/mem thresholds, error-rate delta > 0.5% and latency p99 > 2x baseline.
[05:25] Diego: noted, we'll codify threshold.

[05:28] [Crosstalk] Samir: oh and one more thing — cost. how much will dedicated-like private pilot increment cost when we run high throughput?
[05:33] Maya: for POC pilots we usually bill a predictable flat pilot fee that covers the dedicated nodes for the timeframe; we'll include a showback that maps to tokens and GPU hours. we can run a cost projection based on your peak tp/s.
[05:46] Tara: can we get a per-1000 token burn estimate for the INT8 path vs full fp16?
[05:52] Diego: yes, that'll be in the follow-up matrix — rough ballpark INT8 is 30-40% lower GPU cycles depending on kernel efficiency; we'll quantify with your sample.

[05:59] Maya: okay quick recap of what's committed: 1) Diego will run kernel compatibility matrix and batch simulation; 2) Peregrine to provide sanitized 10k sample and latency traces; 3) Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS integration note; 4) Nina to schedule the 2-hour kernel canary and prepare smoke checklist.
[06:18] Samir: that matches my list. a couple of asks — add a test case for seq len 2k in Diego's matrix and run one noisy neighbor simulation.
[06:27] Diego: will do. noisy neighbor simulation using allocated cgroups to emulate mem pressure, noted.
[06:31] Ben: please include a short write-up on the audit evidence we'll get and the retention window.
[06:36] Maya: yep we'll include that.

[06:40] Nina: next steps and owners are in the doc now, I'll also create calendar invites for the security deep-dive and the canary slot once we have the proposed windows.
[06:49] Samir: target for go/no-go sign off? if the perf matrix and the kernel pass are green we'll schedule the canary the following week.
[06:56] Maya: proposed sign-off by 2027-09-20 so we can plan cutover late September.
[07:01] Samir: sounds reasonable.

Closing:
[07:05] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the security pack. Diego will post the initial compat CSV and Nina will create the canary checklist.
[07:13] Tara: thanks all.
[07:15] Ben: thanks. bye.
